name: Römerweg Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The Roman Way (Römerweg) links Kitzbühel with St. Johann in Tirol, tracing an ancient trade path past historic heritage farmsteads with Kaiser mountain vistas.
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round (prime hiking season April to November)
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Römerweg Kitzbühel (Roman Way) is one of the most culturally evocative and scenic recreational trails in the Kitzbühel Alps, linking the legendary sporting town of Kitzbühel with the market community of St. Johann in Tirol. The trail takes its name from ancient Roman trade routes and packhorse trails that traversed the sunny lower terraces of the Kitzbüheler Horn during antiquity and the Middle Ages, allowing travelers to avoid the marshy floor of the Leukental valley. Hovering between 750 and 850 metres in elevation, the route meanders past centuries-old Tyrolean heritage farmhouses decorated with ornate Lüftlmalerei frescoes and timber carvings. Hikers are treated throughout to unobstructed vistas of the jagged limestone ramparts of the Wilder Kaiser range to the north and rounded green slate ridges to the south.

Route & Anforderungen

The Römerweg is an easy, gratifying trail well suited for families, recreational walkers, and Nordic walkers. Commencing in Kitzbühel, the path traces peaceful agricultural lanes, gravel paths, and meadow fringes through the rural hamlets of Gundhabing and Klausen, passing Oberndorf in Tirol before concluding in St. Johann. Covering roughly ten kilometres with a gentle 150 vertical metres of ascent, the walk requires between 2.5 and 3 hours of leisurely walking. Much of the trail is well-graded, making sections passable with all-terrain strollers or touring bikes. Comfortable walking shoes or trainers with good traction are perfectly adequate; sun protection is recommended due to the open, sunny exposure along the hillsides.

Besuch & Anreise

Arriving by road proceeds via motorway A12 (exit Wörgl-Ost) and the Brixental federal road (B170) straight to Kitzbühel. Public transport logistics are exceptionally convenient: Kitzbühel, Oberndorf, and St. Johann in Tirol all host railway stations on the regional S-Bahn line with half-hourly trains. This setup allows hikers to complete the route in one direction and catch a comfortable five-minute train ride back to their starting point. Public parking lots are available at all rail terminals.

Tipps

Stop at one of the welcoming alpine country inns lining the trail to savor crispy Tyrolean Kaspressknödel dumplings while gazing across at the sheer walls of the Wilder Kaiser. A brief detour to the historic mining chapel at Rerobichl reveals fascinating heritage from medieval copper extraction.
